0x00000116.name: VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE
0x00000116.title: Graphics Driver Hang / Timeout (VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE)
0x00000116.description: Windows detected that the graphics card (GPU) stopped responding and failed to reset within the allotted timeout period (usually 2 seconds).
likelyCauses: GPU driver crash, corruption, or incompatibility
Graphics card is improperly seated in the motherboard PCIe slot or sagging
Loose 12VHPWR or PCIe 8-pin power cables from the power supply
GPU overheating (thermal throttling leading to core halt)
Unstable GPU overclock or undervolt
remediationSteps: Check GPU physical seating: Ensure the GPU is firmly locked into the PCIe x16 slot with the latch clicked, and install a GPU support bracket if sagging.
Check PCIe power cables: Verify all 8-pin / 12VHPWR cables are firmly seated with no bends near the connector.
Perform clean GPU driver reinstall: Use Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Windows Safe Mode, then install the latest official NVIDIA/AMD/Intel driver.
Monitor GPU thermals: Use HWMonitor or MSI Afterburner to ensure GPU core and hotspot temperatures stay below 85°C under load.
Disable unstable overclocks: Reset any GPU/VRAM overclocking software to factory defaults.

0x00000117.name: VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED
0x00000117.title: Graphics Card Video Recovery Timeout
0x00000117.description: The GPU failed to respond to a display command, but Windows attempted a live driver restart.
likelyCauses: Overburdened GPU memory or transient driver glitch
Insufficient PCIe power delivery during peak transient spikes
Background hardware-accelerated app conflict (Discord, Chrome, etc.)
remediationSteps: Update or reinstall graphics drivers.
Disable 'Hardware Acceleration' in Discord/Chrome if crashes occur during multitasking.
Check that your power supply wattage covers your GPU's transient power spikes.

0x00000124.name: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR
0x00000124.title: Fatal Hardware Architecture Error (WHEA)
0x00000124.description: Windows Hardware Error Architecture (WHEA) caught a fatal, non-recoverable hardware fault directly from the CPU, PCIe bus, or memory controllers.
likelyCauses: Unstable CPU voltage or aggressive overclock/undervolt (e.g. Curve Optimizer)
CPU overheating or VRM throttling under heavy load
Faulty NVMe SSD or deteriorating PCIe lane communication
Failing motherboard chipset or CPU core degradation
remediationSteps: Reset BIOS/UEFI settings to Optimized Defaults to disable any unstable CPU/RAM overclocks (XMP/EXPO, PBO, Curve Optimizer).
Check CPU temperatures: Verify CPU cooler pump is running and thermal paste is adequate.
Update Motherboard BIOS to the latest microcode update.
Reseat the primary NVMe SSD and graphics card in their PCIe slots.

0x0000003B.name: SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION
0x0000003B.title: System Service Driver Fault
0x0000003B.description: An executing system service or kernel driver executed an instruction that generated an unhandled exception.
likelyCauses: Corrupt or outdated device drivers (audio, network, or peripheral drivers)
Corrupted Windows system files (e.g., following a forced shutdown)
Conflicting third-party antivirus or kernel-level anti-cheat software
remediationSteps: Run System File Checker: Open PowerShell as Admin and run `sfc /scannow` and `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`.
Update motherboard chipset, audio, and network drivers from manufacturer support page.
Check the minidump faulting module name in technical details to pinpoint the exact driver.

0x000000D1.name: DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
0x000000D1.title: Driver Memory Access Fault (DRIVER_IRQL)
0x000000D1.description: A kernel driver attempted to access pageable memory at an invalid interrupt request level (IRQL).
likelyCauses: Faulty third-party driver attempting illegal memory access
Unstable RAM memory timings or defective memory stick
remediationSteps: Identify the specific driver named in the crash dump (often network, VPN, or audio driver).
Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (`mdsched.exe`) to rule out faulty RAM.
Update or roll back the implicated device driver.

0x0000001A.name: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT
0x0000001A.title: Severe Memory Management Error
0x0000001A.description: A severe memory management error occurred. This is one of the strongest indicators of bad RAM, unstable XMP/EXPO, or dying storage holding the pagefile.
likelyCauses: Failing or degrading physical RAM module
Unstable XMP / DOCP / EXPO memory profile in BIOS
Bad sectors on the drive hosting the Windows pagefile (`pagefile.sys`)
remediationSteps: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic: Press Win+R, type `mdsched.exe`, and choose 'Restart now and check for problems'.
Enter BIOS/UEFI and temporarily disable XMP/EXPO to see if memory stability returns.
Test RAM sticks individually in memory slot A2/B2 to isolate a failing stick.
Check SSD health status in the Storage section of this app.

0x00000050.name: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
0x00000050.title: Invalid Memory Access in Non-Paged Area
0x00000050.description: The system attempted to access invalid system memory that cannot be paged out.
likelyCauses: Faulty RAM hardware or defective motherboard RAM slot
Defective L2/L3 processor cache
Corrupted antivirus or system service driver
remediationSteps: Run a thorough memory test (MemTest86 or Windows Memory Diagnostic).
Reseat all RAM modules firmly into the motherboard slots.
Run `chkdsk C: /f /r` to verify disk file system integrity.

0x00000133.name: DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION
0x00000133.title: DPC Watchdog Timeout Violation
0x00000133.description: A deferred procedure call (DPC) ran for too long, or the system spent too much time at an interrupt level.
likelyCauses: Outdated SSD firmware or corrupted storage AHCI/NVMe controller driver
Conflicting network or Wi-Fi driver hanging the kernel DPC queue
remediationSteps: Update SSD firmware using Samsung Magician, Crucial Storage Executive, or vendor software.
Update the Standard NVM Express Controller or Intel/AMD SATA AHCI driver.
Update Wi-Fi and Ethernet network adapter drivers.

0x0000009F.name: DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE
0x0000009F.title: Driver Power State Transition Failure
0x0000009F.description: A device driver failed to transition between sleep, hibernation, or awake states within the expected time.
likelyCauses: Device driver unable to handle Windows Modern Standby / Sleep states
Peripheral device (USB dock, audio interface, Bluetooth adapter) freezing on wake
remediationSteps: Update all peripheral, Bluetooth, and motherboard chipset drivers.
Disable Fast Startup in Windows Power Options (Control Panel -> Power Options -> Choose what power buttons do -> uncheck 'Turn on fast startup').
Disconnect non-essential external USB hubs to see if sleep crashes cease.

0x000000EF.name: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
0x000000EF.title: Critical Windows Process Terminated
0x000000EF.description: A critical system process required for Windows operation (such as `csrss.exe` or `wininit.exe`) terminated unexpectedly.
likelyCauses: Severe Windows system file corruption
NVMe SSD suddenly disconnecting or failing read operations
Malware interference or corrupted Windows updates
remediationSteps: Run `DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-image /Restorehealth` followed by `sfc /scannow` in Admin PowerShell.
Check NVMe SSD temperature and SMART health in the Storage section.
Check Windows Update history and roll back any recently installed problematic updates.
